name: Thirsting Skull (closed)
beta: A tough, low roof opens the route; beyond it you pump through steeply overhanging stone full of pockets, and a boulder problem guards the chain anchors at the finish.
overview: Pull a demanding low roof, then pump along steep stone riddled with pockets, ending in a bouldery sequence.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the wooden footbridge and keep straight; a branch heads right about 20 feet beyond it. Follow that path uphill roughly ten minutes to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Thrillbillies
beta: From a small pedestal, drift up and to the left via thin runnels, sidepulls, deep horizontal breaks and plates, picking your way over the featured slab to a roomy ledge. Slip off your shoes at the anchors and enjoy the view.
overview: From the pedestal, angle up toward the left past thin water grooves, side-pulls, deep horizontal holds and plates. The featured slab ends on a wide ledge; the anchor is a good place to take shoes off and enjoy the view. Billed as the sequel for anyone who liked Boltergeist.

current.area_walk_in: A signed trail with steps climbs uphill through a pair of switchbacks and meets the wall at its base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: To Defy The Laws Of Tradition
beta: Begin beside a big jumble of boulders and climb the bolted face via little sharp pockets and edges, finishing up a flake that faces right to the chains.
overview: A popular, fingery classic and a first 5.10a for many climbers, on abrasive little pockets and ledges that lead to a flake.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: first route met where the trail reaches the cliff, starting left of a jumble of boulders

name: Too Many Puppies
beta: Step off the boulder pile and stay with the bolted arete throughout, ending at the anchors.
overview: A bolted arete that begins on a boulder pile and runs to cold-shut anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Starts atop a large flat boulder under a big roof; the left-hand of two bolt lines

name: Tower of Power
beta: Begin with pitch one of The Corner, which delivers you under the roof. Stretch way out beyond the lip for a good hold and a perfect 1.5 tricam slot in an upright crack, then pull over and finish on the face higher up, which is rated 5.10.
overview: A rarely climbed, intimidating roof line that follows the opening pitch of a neighbouring route, then a face above the lip.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: reached after climbing The Corner's opening pitch, finishing beneath a daunting roof

name: Blow Me Down
beta: Ascend the thin face beside a neighbouring dihedral, on its left, until you meet a roof's left end at which a crack starts, put in gear at that spot, then complete the climb on another route.
overview: A thin face gains the left side of an overhang, above which a crack starts and gear can be placed. The route then finishes up Shiver Me Timbers.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Thin face immediately left of Arachnid, on level ground at the back of a big rock

name: Green Grease
beta: Begin by following the route before it to the shelf twenty-five feet off the ground, then take the pleasant hand-width split in the face to your right to another ledge. Rappel there, or link into the last pitch of Groundhog to top out.
overview: A three-star hand crack on a right-hand face, reached by climbing the preceding route to a ledge; it can be rappelled or continued toward the summit.

current.descent: rappel from that ledge, or continue up Groundhog's final pitch
current.location: follow Curving Crack to its ledge 25 ft up, then take the hand crack in the right-hand face

name: Heart of Darkness
beta: It shares a face with its neighbour South of Zimbabwe, though past the bolt it angles upward and rightward to horizontal breaks. Get gear in, follow a flake, then pull hard to the top; carry small nuts and cams.
overview: Gear goes into horizontal breaks; a flake follows, and a final hard pull finishes it.

current.descent: as for South of Zimbabwe
current.location: shares South of Zimbabwe's face but trends rightwards and upwards after the bolt

name: Shiver Me Timbers
beta: Start with the clean first dihedral of the neighbouring route, then traverse leftward along a shelf under the roof on the left. Place gear, then follow the faint corner and rounded edge to the anchors. Pitch two crosses the wall to the big ledge.
overview: A two-pitch trad route that begins up a neighbouring route's clean dihedral, then crosses left beneath a roof before continuing up a faint corner and arete.

current.location: Starts up the clean first dihedral of Arachnid

name: Trad Sucker
beta: Clamber up onto boulders to start, then pass iron-hard jugs and a low empty bolt hole before slanting leftward to the chain anchors beneath a high roof.
overview: Scramble up a few boulders to reach hard-edged iron jugs, pass a bolt hole close to the ground, then trend up-left to anchors tucked beneath a big roof.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the first rockhouse's left flank, around the arete from One-Eyed Willy

name: Trinket Man
beta: Gain the ledge via four bolts on the green wall below, take a breather there, then launch onto the bolted arete, which ends at an anchor close to the rim.
overview: The leftmost of several bolted lines reached from a ledge, finishing along a bolted arete near the crest of the wall; ten bolts in all.

current.area_walk_in: A steep trail leads uphill from the pulloff to the cliff. It is distinct at the start but easy to lose, so follow it carefully to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: leftmost of several bolted routes off a ledge reached by climbing a green wall past four bolts, up the trail right of Yuk

name: Trust in Jesus
beta: Share the opening of Injured: step onto a low boulder shaped like a ledge and find two bolts side by side. Go directly to the left one, then clip the right one, and slant upward to the right across gray, platy stone to the quick-link anchors.
overview: Shares its opening with Injured Reserve, clipping the left bolt then the right. It then trends up and rightward over sharp grey plates with some demanding moves.

current.area_walk_in: From the parking lot, follow the trail system toward the Motherlode and take the left-hand fork.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Last of the bolted routes on the Warm-up Wall, sharing its start with Injured Reserve

name: Tuna Town
beta: Begin left of a chest-high flake that faces left. Pass a large hueco ledge on its left side onto a platform atop a small pillar, then tackle very steep rock beside a short, overhanging dihedral, aiming for a horizontal shelf. A greenish section follows, then an orange featured stretch leads to the chain anchor.
overview: A big hueco shelf on the left leads onto a small pillar perch. The line then follows a short steep corner up very steep stone to a ledge, and finishes across a greenish stretch and an orange-coloured band.

current.area_walk_in: Walk toward the right from Madness Cave to reach a lower, less steep wall holding many lines. The first line met is The Sauce, beside a large tree that grows against the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Starts just beyond a thin chest-high flake that angles up toward the right

name: Sideshow
beta: Stay on the face beside the obtuse dihedral rather than in the dihedral itself, and protect with natural gear.
overview: Climbs the face next to an open-book corner using natural gear.

current.area_walk_in: Hike uphill with the big roof off to your left until a short blocky dihedral gives access to a terrace; the steep crack lies a bit farther left along it.
current.descent: walk left to the little corner that serves as the approach to Negative Energy
current.location: Obtuse dihedral about 150 ft past the little corner you scale to reach Negative Energy, heading right

name: Twin Cracks
beta: Start in the right-hand crack of the pair, then switch left partway and fight a pump onto the ledge. Lower off fixed gear.
overview: Two parallel cracks make up the line. You get going in the right-hand one, shift over to the other, and push through to the ledge up top.

current.area_walk_in: Stay beside the river on the path for roughly half a mile, passing a couple of caves and old fire rings. Cross a small side stream, reach a broad level clearing, then bear left off the main path onto an old overgrown track that climbs toward the wall. At the wall, go left where the path divides.
current.descent: lower from fixed gear

name: Unsportsmanlike Conduct
beta: Start from the boulder fronting the route, step across and enter the split, hanging tight for roughly fifteen feet. Higher, a pod and assorted odd features lead to the ledge at the top; you belay using the anchors of the neighbouring route.
overview: Transfer from the boulder to the crack and remain in it around 15 feet, then continue via a pod and assorted awkward moves to a finish ledge. Belay at the anchors shared with Stunning the Hog.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Past the next buttress after Birthday Party, a crack runs through an overhanging face; get started from the boulder fronting it

name: Vector Trouble
beta: Follow the left-hand crack of the pair to a ledge about twenty-five feet up, then carry on along the slim corner under a last roof. Either chimney the slot or exit rightward on face holds. Descend by rappelling off the ledge, or add the brief second pitch to reach the summit.
overview: Pick the leftmost of the paired cracks to gain a ledge some 25 feet up, then the slim corner to a last roof, which goes either by chimneying a slot or by exiting right to face holds. Lower from that ledge, or tack on a brief extra pitch for the top out.

current.area_walk_in: A steep trail leads uphill from the pulloff to the cliff. It is distinct at the start but easy to lose, so follow it carefully to the wall.
current.descent: lower from that ledge, or finish with a brief extra pitch to the top
current.location: Beyond Long Wall Chimney to the left, an orange corner topped by a crack that flares

name: Chemical Imbalance
beta: Start on the slab beside a neighbouring bolted line, clip three bolts, then switch to small and medium cams for the stretch leading to the ledge.
overview: Once a purely gear-protected line, it was later given bolts for safety. Climb the slab past the bolts, then complete the climb to the ledge on small to medium cams.

current.area_walk_in: A flat, well-made trail winds through pleasant surroundings; this is among the longer walks in the area. The cliff is reached by that path, and a line of bolts runs up the main arete to your left as you arrive.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Slab alongside Toxic Avenger on its right

name: Double Trouble
beta: Take the right-hand crack until it dies out, then work along the thin wall onto a ledge. Easier face climbing leads from there to the bolted anchors.
overview: A four-star trad line starting up twin cracks under a small roof, finishing on easier face to bolted anchors.

current.area_walk_in: A flat, well-made trail winds through pleasant surroundings; this is among the longer walks in the area. The cliff is reached by that path, and a line of bolts runs up the main arete to your left as you arrive.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: two cracks below a little roof some 15 ft up, 30 ft beyond Apehouse after turning a corner

name: Drug Pusher
beta: Climb to a horizontal break and place gear, then stretch out, let go and crank past the lip of the eight-foot roof into a slot of offwidth size. A finger crack leads from there to the fixed anchors.
overview: Climb to a horizontal break and place gear, then reach out under the roof and swing around the edge and into a wide slot. A finger crack takes you the rest of the way to fixed anchors.

current.area_walk_in: A flat, well-made trail winds through pleasant surroundings; this is among the longer walks in the area. The cliff is reached by that path, and a line of bolts runs up the main arete to your left as you arrive.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Walk beyond Must Dihedral to a crack under an 8-ft roof that sits about 15 ft off the ground

name: Testosterone Testpiece
beta: Climb the offwidth to the perch, then either rappel off the tree or move across leftward to continue on the neighbouring route's second pitch.

current.area_walk_in: A flat, well-made trail winds through pleasant surroundings; this is among the longer walks in the area. The cliff is reached by that path, and a line of bolts runs up the main arete to your left as you arrive.
current.descent: abseil from the tree on the ledge, or cross leftward onto pitch two of Hair of the Dog
current.location: Offwidth a few ft beyond Hair of the Dog on the right

name: Which is Which
beta: A steep start gets you onto a ledge for the hands, the face above is more vertical, and the overhanging headwall at the top is the final test before the chains.
overview: A two-star sport line with a steep start, a more vertical middle and an overhanging headwall.

current.area_walk_in: This cliff sits a short distance beyond the neighbouring wall called The Playground, tucked behind a bend; expect lengthy, leaning, pocket-rich routes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 10 ft over from Who Knows?

name: Who is Who
beta: Begin a few feet over from the previous route and pull on pockets for four bolts to reach a vertical section. Pass it, then deal with the increasingly steep rock above.
overview: A two-star sport line on a steep section of wall: pocket-pulling to a vertical stretch, then rock that keeps steepening.

current.area_walk_in: This cliff sits a short distance beyond the neighbouring wall called The Playground, tucked behind a bend; expect lengthy, leaning, pocket-rich routes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 5 ft past Which is Which, same steep part of the wall

name: Who Knows?
beta: Two bolts of steep rock bring you to a big ledge; a chunky flake leads to a second ledge, and steeper rock above takes you to the anchors.
overview: A two-star sport route over steep rock with two ledges, a fat flake between them, and steeper stone above.

current.area_walk_in: This cliff sits a short distance beyond the neighbouring wall called The Playground, tucked behind a bend; expect lengthy, leaning, pocket-rich routes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 20 ft along from Crucify Me

name: Who Pooped in the Park?
beta: Start via the crack when it is dry, otherwise the face on its left. Abandon the large holds and step right to clip bolt two, find a rest above, then bust up the brief, pumpy headwall on single-pad edges.
overview: Start in the crack if dry, otherwise on the adjacent face, then step right off the big holds for the second clip. A rest follows, then a short, pumpy headwall of edges.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Animal Crackers trail and keep going several hundred feet past that wall to a steep ravine beside a large amphitheater. Descend the sandy ravine, step across a little creek at the bottom, then go a short way up and around a corner to the overhanging main wall. The routes at the far end lie about 100 feet beyond it.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Wildfire
beta: Begin on a boulder and step into a traverse that angles up and right, then go directly upward through the fingery wall, make the final clip and blast the last stretch to the chains.
overview: A five-star, fingertip-intense sport line on the steeper, less featured right-hand side of an orange wall, starting from a boulder.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: on the steeper, plainer right-hand part of the wall; starts from a boulder about 10 ft past the neighbouring route

name: Wobbler
beta: A handful of big moves start things, then it is a race through connected pockets and little crimps. Nothing gives a rest, and a short roof comes right before the chains, so a fall there means starting over.
overview: A two-star sport line made of linked pockets and tiny crimps and offering no real rest, ending over a small roof.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the dirt track uphill until it bends, then keep straight onto a footpath that leads to the cliff; side logging tracks branch off toward the left-hand routes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: bolted line nearest the Mad Hatter crack, on its right

name: Zambezi Plunge
beta: Follow the hand crack up to a shelf with a big boulder and a tree, then keep going up the wide section to the anchors of the neighbouring route.
overview: The first route ever climbed at the crag: a hand crack set in a little corner that leads to a ledge, then an offwidth.

current.area_walk_in: A switchbacking trail climbs the hillside and ends directly below the conspicuous pinnacle holding The Arrowhead.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Cereal Killer
beta: Most parties stop after pitch one since higher sections are dirty. Layback the flake, step around the roof's left end, and clip a few more bolts to the chains.
overview: Normally only the first pitch is led, as later pitches are grubby. It starts with a layback up a flake facing right, then pulls round the left tip of the small overhang on bolts to chains on a ledge.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the trail along the cliff base downhill, below the Practice Wall, passing under an extended low roof; these routes begin at that roof's far right end.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 20 ft out from the roof's right-hand portion

name: Crank it to Eleven
beta: Follow a swept strip across a sharply angled slab, and a bulge, up to the anchors beneath the big roof, with pitch two then continuing past it.
overview: A thin face climb up a cleared stripe on a steep slab, crossing a bulge and ending at anchors under the roof. There is also a second pitch that wraps round the overhang up to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: beneath the right-hand end of the large roof on the right

name: Blaze of Glory
beta: Steep, rewarding movement on good holds follows a broken pale streak. A bolted slab leads first to a roof, after which the rock becomes blockier and steeper along a dike.
overview: Superb, steep and sustained on positive holds, following a fractured pale stripe. A bolted slab leads to a roof, above which the rock steepens and turns blocky along a dike.

current.descent: rappel with two ropes, or lower on a 60 m rope

name: Desperado
beta: Pitch one heads up and left over a small roof, then continues over solid stone to a bolt and on to an easier slab. Pitch two climbs a corner, then moves rightward across a face to a tree.
overview: A serious, runout line on excellent rock. The first pitch climbs a stubby horizontal slot beyond a small overhang, then relies on face moves with poor protection until a bolt well up the wall. The second pitch follows a corner and swings rightward to the wall.

current.area_walk_in: A trail enters the woods and right away swings hard left, then meanders uphill beyond a low cliff to the foot of Charlotte's Crack. Veering right instead ends in a boulder field, which means you are off the path.
current.location: starts at the tree on Belay Seat Ledge, right of The Arete

name: Faust
beta: Start with the bottom slab to the bolted belay, then angle up and left across simple rock toward a brief dihedral. Stem it, surmount a bulge using a finger crack, and finish via steep fractured cracks.
overview: Starts from the bolted belay above the lower slab. Easy ground leads leftward to a short corner that is stemmed, followed by a bulge split by a finger crack, and steep, fractured cracks complete it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: begins at the belay anchors on top of the lower slab, then trends left over easy ground

name: The Cold War
beta: Edge your way left up the black slab, passing four bolts, then escape left beneath the roof via a crack you can hand-traverse to the anchor.
overview: A sport line over a black slab finishing by a leftward crack traverse under a roof to the anchor.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 30 ft right of the first route on the wall (Bongs Away)

name: Too Close For Comfort
beta: A delicate face climb past six bolts on a steep slab, finishing in the awkward, moss-covered dihedral near the top.
overview: Technical face climbing up the steep slab beside the streak, finishing in an awkward corner coated in lichen, which ends at the cliff top. Modest-sized protection is wanted in the upper corner.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left of a dark streak and over a slab beneath a prominent corner that angles left

name: High Noon
beta: Smear along the black streak's right side past five bolts to the corner that angles left, pull over a roof on the right, then use a crack angling right to reach the steep headwall.
overview: A sustained, excellent line and one of this crag's best, which finishes up a steep headwall.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: tracking a dark streak on its right-hand flank up to a left-leaning corner

name: Sales Pitch
beta: Use delicate face moves, clipping three bolts.
overview: A thin face route that begins beside a small maple on the ledge's right side and passes three bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: beside a small maple on the right-hand part of the ledge

name: White Streak
beta: Pitch one follows intermittent cracks and corners beside a thin white stripe. Pitch two edges up that steep, featureless-looking wall, protected by Tricams plus Friends placed in pockets, and eases toward the top.
overview: Sustained, high-quality face climbing alongside a pale streak. The first pitch links thin cracks and corners; the second edges right up the wall and eases near the top.

current.area_walk_in: A trail enters the woods and right away swings hard left, then meanders uphill beyond a low cliff to the foot of Charlotte's Crack. Veering right instead ends in a boulder field, which means you are off the path.
current.location: from Belay Seat Ledge

name: Cell Phones and Fast Food
beta: Haul on jugs through a succession of small overhangs with good gear throughout; scramble the small ledges toward the first overhang, then keep following solid holds across four overhangs up to a belay on a large boulder. Bring cams to 3 inches.
overview: A jug-haul through four small overhangs, with good protection all the way. Small ledges lead into the lowest overhang, then positive holds link the rest up to a boulder sitting on a broad ledge.

current.location: starts at a tree hugging the cliff base, a bit west of Faint's Roof

name: Fever Dream
beta: Start facing the big tree used as a belay anchor, go directly to the overhang, then power and smear beyond the roof, just rightward of a minuscule corner.
overview: A very hard toprope up to a roof where a pair of minute underclings sit partway out.
